title: Mixed-effects deep learning diagnoses COVID-19 from CT, externally validated in China
summary: A deep learning model with a mixed-effects layer modeling slice relationships was trained on CT volumes from 1,110 patients in Moscow and externally validated on 796 patients from a Chinese consortium (CC-CCII). External AUROC was 0.936 (95% CI 0.910-0.961), with sensitivity 0.753 and specificity 0.909 at a 0.5 threshold; calibration, decision-curve analysis and saliency maps were also assessed. Data were collected retrospectively in early 2020. Preprint of 2022-01-30.
ai_technology: Deep learning model with a mixed-effects layer on CT volumes to diagnose COVID-19
